recommendations.recommendation: Do not waste effort trying to win over a fool puffed up with a little learning; he cannot be persuaded.
recommendations.rationale: The ignorant and the wise are easily pleased, but not even the creator can satisfy a half-learned conceited man; impossible feats are easier.
recommendations.argued_against: the conceited, half-learned fool

recommendations.recommendation: Treasure learning above all other wealth.
recommendations.rationale: Learning is hidden wealth thieves cannot steal, grows when given away, earns honor from kings, and helps abroad; without it a man is a beast.
recommendations.argued_against: the unlearned man who lives like an animal without horns or tail

recommendations.recommendation: Seek the company of good and virtuous people.
recommendations.rationale: Good company clears dullness of mind, inclines speech to truth, raises honor, removes sin, gladdens the heart, and spreads fame.
recommendations.argued_against: none

recommendations.recommendation: Shun a wicked person even if he is learned.
recommendations.rationale: A serpent adorned with a jewel is no less dangerous; learning does not make the wicked safe.
recommendations.argued_against: learned but wicked people

recommendations.recommendation: Once you begin a worthy undertaking, persist no matter how often obstacles strike.
recommendations.rationale: Low people never start for fear of obstacles, middling people quit when blocked, but the best never abandon what they began even when struck repeatedly.
recommendations.argued_against: those who never begin or who give up at the first obstacle

recommendations.recommendation: Keep to the path of justice whether you are praised or blamed, rich or poor, and whether death comes today or much later.
recommendations.rationale: The steadfast never take a step away from the righteous path, whatever the outcome.
recommendations.argued_against: none

recommendations.recommendation: Cultivate refined speech as your true ornament rather than relying on jewelry and adornment.
recommendations.rationale: Bracelets, necklaces, baths, perfumes, and flowers do not truly adorn a man; other ornaments perish, while cultured speech endures.
recommendations.argued_against: reliance on outward ornaments

recommendations.recommendation: Give or enjoy your wealth rather than hoarding it.
recommendations.rationale: Wealth has 3 possible fates, giving, enjoyment, or loss; whoever neither gives nor enjoys it will meet the third.
recommendations.argued_against: misers who neither give nor enjoy

recommendations.recommendation: Serve the good of others even at cost to yourself, unasked, as the sun opens lotuses and clouds give rain.
recommendations.rationale: The noble help others unbidden and set aside their own interest; those who ruin others for gain are demons, and those who do it for nothing are worse.
recommendations.argued_against: those who harm others for their own gain or for no gain at all

recommendations.recommendation: Preserve your honor and self-respect even in hardship rather than stooping to baseness.
recommendations.rationale: A lion, though starving, aged, and weak, will not eat grass but seeks the elephant; the high-minded likewise keep their dignity.
recommendations.argued_against: those who give up dignity to survive

recommendations.recommendation: Value friendship with the good and recognize a true friend by his conduct.
recommendations.rationale: A true friend keeps you from wrong, leads you to good, hides your secrets, shows your virtues, stays in misfortune, and gives in need; such friendship grows like the afternoon shadow.
recommendations.argued_against: friendship of the wicked, which starts large and shrinks like the morning shadow

recommendations.recommendation: Revere the power of karma, recognizing that the fruits of action govern even the gods.
recommendations.rationale: Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva are themselves bound to their tasks by karma, so karma deserves homage.
recommendations.argued_against: none

recommendations.recommendation: Recognize that craving never grows old though you do, and stop letting it consume you.
recommendations.rationale: We did not enjoy pleasures, they devoured us; time did not pass, we passed; craving stayed young while we aged.
recommendations.argued_against: a life spent chasing sensual pleasure

recommendations.recommendation: Embrace dispassion, since every worldly good carries fear and only detachment is free of it.
recommendations.rationale: Pleasure fears disease, family fears decline, wealth fears kings, honor fears humiliation, learning fears rivals, the body fears death; only renunciation is fearless.
recommendations.argued_against: trust in pleasure, lineage, wealth, honor, learning, beauty, or the body

recommendations.recommendation: Work for your soul's welfare while the body is healthy and old age far off, before death approaches.
recommendations.rationale: Beginning when life is ebbing is like digging a well after the house is already on fire.
recommendations.conditions: while body and senses are still sound
recommendations.argued_against: postponing spiritual effort until old age

recommendations.recommendation: Do not fawn on the rich or beg favors at the doors of proud kings.
recommendations.rationale: Servility to arrogant masters is humiliating and futile, while the forest freely offers fruit, water, and a bed of earth.
recommendations.argued_against: flatterers and courtiers who serve the wealthy for gain

recommendations.recommendation: Be content with a simple life in which earth is your bed, your arm your pillow, and the sky your roof.
recommendations.rationale: The contented sage lives as happily as a king on what nature provides, while the discontented are never satisfied.
recommendations.argued_against: restless pursuit of wealth and status

recommendations.recommendation: Remember that youth, wealth, and life are fleeting, like waves and lightning.
recommendations.rationale: All worldly things pass swiftly, so clinging to them is folly.
recommendations.argued_against: attachment to transient things

recommendations.recommendation: Fix your mind on Shiva and the Supreme rather than on sense objects.
recommendations.rationale: Only the Supreme gives lasting peace, while sense pleasures are brief and lead to sorrow.
recommendations.argued_against: absorption in women and worldly delights

recommendations.recommendation: Recognize that the worthy paths are wholehearted love or the forest life of renunciation.
recommendations.rationale: The poet presents the embrace of a beloved and devotion in a forest retreat as the 2 things truly worth having.
recommendations.argued_against: none

recommendations.recommendation: Recognize how a woman's charms can bewitch and bind even wise men.
recommendations.rationale: Desire overpowers judgment so that even the learned are captured by a glance, and this bondage ends in suffering.
recommendations.argued_against: the deluded lover
